$comment: Declarative tables for the two fire-spread animations. The original had eight near-identical functions (animatePhase1..4 and animateExistingPhase1..4) that looked interchangeable but were not: they differ in duration, scaling, offset growth and -- critically -- in where each phase's opening shape comes from. Encoding those differences as data makes the divergence explicit instead of something you have to diff by eye.

geometry.$comment_wind: Each vertex radius is multiplied by 1 + amplitude*cos(vertexAngle - windDirection), clamped, so the blob stretches downwind. Clamps keep the shape convex-ish rather than collapsing to a crescent.
geometry.$comment_projection: Flat-earth approximation, adequate at the few-kilometre scale of a single fire. 111320 m is one degree of latitude; longitude degrees shrink by cos(latitude), derived from the 40075000 m equatorial circumference.

polygonStyle.$comment: Shared Leaflet style for every fire polygon. Stroke and fill always share a colour; only the colour changes per phase.

$comment_reorder: After the last phase the stack is re-fronted smallest-first so earlier, tighter polygons stay visible above the later, larger ones. The short delay lets Leaflet finish the final render first.

clicked.$comment: Runs when the user clicks empty map. Slow (7 s a phase) and continuous: phases 2-4 open exactly where the previous phase closed, so the blob morphs without ever jumping.

phases.$comment: Pure scale-up with no colour change and no offset growth. This is the only phase in either sequence that recomputes vertices from scale each frame rather than interpolating between two vertex lists.
startFrom 'previous' is what makes this sequence continuous: the new polygon is drawn on the closing vertices of the phase before it.
Final phase: no nextAngleOffset, so the runner stops and triggers the re-order instead of chaining.

existing.$comment: Runs from the Simulate Fire button on a real EONET event. Faster (3 s a phase), grows by much larger offsets, and never scales -- the starting radius already comes from the event's reported acreage, so all growth is expressed through the offsets.
existing.$comment_baseRadius: Deliberately absent: this sequence's base radius is the event's own impact radius, supplied per-call.

phases.$comment: startFrom 'recomputed' reproduces the original faithfully: every phase rebuilds its opening vertices from the current offsets at the CURRENT angle offset. Because each phase draws a fresh angle, the shape visibly snaps at every phase boundary. That jump is in the shipped behaviour and is preserved on purpose, not an artefact of this refactor.
